title: Capture profile
description: One feed app, and how to scroll it. Read-only by construction: no like/follow/comment/DM verb exists in this schema.
comment: Kind-specific requirements (mirror needs app/capture/actions/abort, feed needs sources) are enforced in scripts/lib/profile.mjs, which reports them in plain language.

name.description: Profile id. Used as `--profile <name>` and in the digest filename.

app.description: App name as it appears in iOS Spotlight, used to launch it inside the mirror.

kind.description: mirror = screenshots via iPhone Mirroring. feed = text over HTTP, no phone involved.

description.description: What this feed is for, in one line. Shows up in the digest header.

maxFrames.description: Hard ceiling on frames. Each frame costs vision tokens — budget deliberately.

maxMinutes.description: Wall-clock ceiling. Whichever limit hits first ends the run.

dwellMs.description: Pause after each scroll. Human pace, and gives the feed time to render.

scrollTicks.description: Scroll wheel ticks per step. Video feeds want a full-screen jump; text feeds want less.

settleMs.description: Extra wait after launching the app, before the first frame.

downscaleWidth.description: Frames are resized to this width before Claude reads them. Lower = cheaper.

bannerStripPx.description: Top band blanked on every frame so notification banners are never recorded.

hammingThreshold.description: Perceptual-hash distance below which a frame is treated as a repeat and dropped.

lookback.description: How many recent frames a new frame is compared against.

actions.description: Everything the run is permitted to do. tap:navOnly means taps confined to the navigation regions declared in navTargets.

navTargets.description: Named tap points as fractions of the mirror window, e.g. "followingTab": [0.72, 0.11]. Only these coordinates are tappable.

stuckFrames.description: Identical frames in a row before giving up — means mirroring paused, the phone was picked up, or the feed ended.

blankFrames.description: Near-uniform frames in a row before giving up — means a black DRM surface or a disconnected session.

readerStopOn.description: If Claude sees any of these while reading frames, it stops the run and deletes the remaining frames. Enforced at read time, not by pixels.

sources.description: Only for kind=feed. Text sources fetched over HTTP — no phone, no vision tokens.

interests.description: Topics that push an item up the digest. Everything else is summarised as noise.
